results.typed: Explain how a VPN works in simple words

results.expect: one reply, no duplicate bubbles, sensible tone and casing
results.lastReply:
A VPN is a private tunnel between your device and the internet, so nobody in between can see what you send.

Normally, your data travels through your Wi-Fi and your internet company, and they can see which sites you visit. With a VPN, your device locks (encrypts) everything first and sends it to the VPN company's computer. That computer unlocks it and talks to the website for you.

What that means for you:

On public Wi-Fi: strangers on the same network can't read your traffic.
Your location: websites see the VPN computer's address, not yours.
The catch: the VPN company can now see your traffic instead, so pick one you trust. It also doesn't protect you from fake sites or bad downloads.
